plan.headline: Compare ticket volume by category in the week of Aug 10, 2026 against the prior weeks to find which category spiked.

metrics.title: Tickets by category in spike week
metrics.description: Number of support tickets created in the selected spike week, grouped by category, shown next to the baseline weekly average for the same category so the spike is visible.

metrics.title: Spike vs baseline
metrics.description: For each category, tickets in the spike week divided by the average weekly tickets over the baseline weeks before it. A ratio well above 1 means the category spiked.

metrics.title: Weekly tickets by category
metrics.description: Weekly count of tickets created per category over the trend period, to show the spike in context.

assumptions.label: Spike week start
assumptions.rationale: The week of August 10, 2026 starts on Monday, Aug 10, and runs through Sunday, Aug 16.

assumptions.label: Trend period
assumptions.rationale: Roughly 6 months of weekly data gives context before and after the spike week.

assumptions.label: Baseline weeks
assumptions.rationale: Number of weeks before the spike week averaged as the normal level for comparison.

assumptions.label: Timezone
assumptions.rationale: Ticket timestamps are stored in UTC, so weeks are bucketed in a single chosen timezone.

assumptions.label: Exclude test orgs
assumptions.rationale: Test, QA and demo tenants are not real customers and would distort ticket counts.

events.sql: WITH tix AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', t.created_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date AS wk, t.category FROM northwind.support_tickets t JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id WHERE t.created_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND t.created_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)) SELECT wk AS x, COUNT(*)::numeric AS y, category AS series FROM tix GROUP BY wk, category ORDER BY wk, category

events.sql:
WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT
    (:spike_week_start_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS spike_start,
    (:spike_week_start_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS spike_end,
    ((:spike_week_start_start::date)::timestamp - make_interval(days => :baseline_weeks::int * 7)) AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS base_start
),
tickets AS (
  SELECT t.category, t.created_at
  FROM northwind.support_tickets t
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id
  WHERE (:exclude_test_accounts::boolean = false OR o.is_test = false)
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    t.category,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.created_at >= b.spike_start AND t.created_at < b.spike_end) AS spike_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.created_at >= b.base_start AND t.created_at < b.spike_start) AS baseline_count
  FROM tickets t
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
  WHERE t.created_at >= b.base_start AND t.created_at < b.spike_end
  GROUP BY t.category
)
SELECT
  category AS label,
  spike_count AS value,
  round(baseline_count::numeric / :baseline_weeks::int, 1) AS baseline_weekly_avg
FROM agg
ORDER BY value DESC, label
LIMIT 20
events.explanation: Counts tickets per category created in the spike week (timezone-adjusted, test orgs optionally excluded) alongside the average weekly count over the preceding baseline weeks.

WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT
    (:spike_week_start_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS spike_start,
    (:spike_week_start_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS spike_end,
    ((:spike_week_start_start::date) - (:baseline_weeks::int * 7))::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS base_start
),
tickets AS (
  SELECT t.category, t.created_at
  FROM northwind.support_tickets t
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id
  WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
),
per_category AS (
  SELECT
    t.category,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.created_at >= b.spike_start AND t.created_at < b.spike_end) AS spike_tickets,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.created_at >= b.base_start AND t.created_at < b.spike_start) AS baseline_tickets
  FROM tickets t
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
  GROUP BY t.category
)
SELECT
  category,
  spike_tickets,
  round(baseline_tickets::numeric / :baseline_weeks::int, 1) AS baseline_weekly_avg,
  round(spike_tickets::numeric / NULLIF(baseline_tickets::numeric / :baseline_weeks::int, 0), 2) AS spike_ratio
FROM per_category
ORDER BY spike_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, spike_tickets DESC

review.summary: The weekly trend is counted correctly and excludes test orgs, but the first and last weeks of the range are partial, so they will look like false dips next to the full weeks.

issues.message: date_trunc('week', created_at) buckets include partial weeks: 2026-04-27 has only 5 days, and 2026-10-26 is cut off by the range end and the data end (2026-10-27). Clip the range to whole Monday-start weeks.
Weeks where a category has zero tickets produce no row, so that series line skips over the gap instead of dropping to 0. Zero-fill with generate_series over weeks × categories if gaps matter.
